**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73817, Reactome:R-HSA-9679191, Reactome:R-HSA-9748787, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

Loss-of-function mutations in IMPDH1 impair guanosine monophosphate (GMP) production, disrupting purine biosynthesis. This disruption leads to both retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital amaurosis due to the critical role of purine metabolism in photoreceptor and retinal ganglion cell function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in IMPDH1 that result in a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if no significant impairment in purine biosynthesis is observed in cells with IMPDH1 mutations linked to these diseases, the proposed mechanism would be refuted. _(variant: None)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving IMPDH1 and purine biosynthesis could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic pathways to treat both retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital amaurosis.
